title: Car Fleet II
statement:
Cars drive in one direction along a single-lane road and are treated as points on a number line. `cars[i] = [position_i, speed_i]` gives car `i`'s starting distance from the start of the road (in meters) and its starting speed (in meters per second); the positions strictly increase with `i`.

When two cars reach the same point they collide and merge into one fleet: from then on they share a single position and move at the speed of the slowest car that started in that fleet.

Return an array `answer` where `answer[i]` is the time in seconds when car `i` collides with car `i + 1` (the next car ahead), or `-1` if that never happens. Answers within `10^-5` of the true values are accepted.
notes:
## Intuition

Simulating every merge works but is slow and fiddly. Look at car `i` from behind: it can only ever hit cars ahead of it, and those cars' futures do not depend on it. So process cars from right to left. Car `i` reaches the fleet ahead at the moment it reaches some specific car `ahead` *while that car still drives at its own speed*, that is, no later than `answer[ahead]`. Until then `ahead` is a straight line `aheadPosition + aheadSpeed · t`, so the meeting time is a simple division. A stack keeps only the cars that could still be that first contact.

## Approach

1. Walk `i` from the last car to the first, with an empty `stack` of candidate indices.
2. Look at the top car `ahead`. If it is at least as fast as car `i`, car `i` can never catch it (or anything that only it shields), so pop it.
3. Otherwise compute `time = (aheadPosition - position) / (speed - aheadSpeed)`. If `ahead` already merged before that moment (`answer[ahead] !== -1` and `time > answer[ahead]`), it has slowed down and is no longer a straight line; pop it and try the car it merged into.
4. Otherwise `time` is the answer for car `i`; stop.
5. Push `i`: it may be the first contact for cars further back.

## Example 1, step by step

`cars = [[1,2],[2,1],[4,3],[7,2]]`.

- `i = 3`: stack empty, `answer[3] = -1`; stack `[3]`.
- `i = 2` (speed 3) vs car 3 (speed 2): `time = (7 - 4) / 1 = 3`, and car 3 never merges, so `answer[2] = 3`; stack `[3, 2]`.
- `i = 1` (speed 1): car 2 and car 3 are faster, both popped; `answer[1] = -1`; stack `[1]`.
- `i = 0` (speed 2) vs car 1 (speed 1): `time = (2 - 1) / 1 = 1`; `answer[0] = 1`.

Result: `[1, -1, 3, -1]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is pushed once and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack and the answer.

## Pitfalls

- Equal speeds never collide; pop on `speed <= aheadSpeed`, not just `<`, or you divide by zero.
- Checking only the next car is wrong: once it merges it slows down, so you must compare with `answer[ahead]`.
- Return times as floating-point numbers; integer division loses the fractional part.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `answer` | collision time of each car with the one ahead, or -1 |
| `stack` | indices of cars ahead that could still be the first contact |
| `position`, `speed` | car `i`'s start and speed |
| `ahead` | index on top of the stack being tested |
| `aheadPosition`, `aheadSpeed` | that car's start and own speed |
| `time` | when car `i` would reach `ahead` if `ahead` kept its speed |

narration.3: Every car starts as 'never collides'; only cars that find a target get a time.
narration.4: The stack holds indices of cars ahead that might still be the first one car i hits.
narration.6: Process cars from the front of the road backwards, so everything ahead is already solved.
narration.8: Keep testing candidates until one works or none are left.
narration.11: A car ahead that is as fast or faster can never be caught by car i.
narration.12: Drop it: it cannot be the first contact for car i or any car behind it that is no faster.
narration.15: Assuming the car ahead keeps its own speed, this is when car i reaches it.
narration.16: If the car ahead merged before that moment, it slowed down and the straight-line time is invalid.
narration.17: Drop it and test the car it merged into, which is next on the stack.
narration.20: The car ahead is still on its own line at that time, so this is car i's collision time.
narration.23: Car i becomes a candidate for the cars behind it.
